I’m 54 this year, been farming since I was 19. Never went to school, can’t read the words on the fertilizer bag, but I know my land. I’ve got 12 mu total — 8 mu for wheat then maize, and 4 mu for cotton. Five people at home and money’s always tight, so I don’t try new things. I watch what my neighbors do and stick with what got us through last year.

**Winter wheat (8 mu):** I plant in early October, same time as everyone in the village. I buy improved wheat seed from the shop in town, about 40 yuan per mu. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — I don’t weigh it on a scale, but it’s roughly half a big bag per mu, about 15 kg of nitrogen total when you add in the topdress. At jointing time in spring, if the wheat looks a little yellow, I spread urea on top. I irrigate three times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once in March when the wheat wakes up, and once at grain filling. Pumping costs money, so I don’t water more than I have to. My husband and I do most of the work, and I might hire someone for a day or two at harvest if we’re rushing. Last year I got about 420 kg per mu; if the weather is normal I expect the same.

**Summer maize (8 mu):** Planted right after wheat harvest in mid-June. Sometimes we cut wheat in the morning and put maize in the same afternoon — the window is very tight. I have to buy hybrid seed every year, can’t save it, costs about 50 yuan per mu. I put fertilizer down at planting, about 14 kg of nitrogen per mu total for the season, maybe one more shot later if it rains well. Two irrigations, at the big growth stages. I spray herbicide once. We mostly harvest by hand or hire a machine if the price is right. Expecting around 480 kg per mu.

**Cotton (4 mu):** Planted in late April. It needs a lot of picking work — my daughter-in-law and I do most of it, going back four or five times as the bolls open. I put less fertilizer than wheat, about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu, in two goes. But I spray more for bugs, especially the bollworm — it was bad two years ago so I keep insecticide ready. I irrigate twice, at flowering and when the bolls are setting. Cotton brings decent cash when prices hold up, so I keep those 4 mu. Hoping for about 230 kg per mu after ginning.

I don’t like changing what works. Last year was okay — not great, not terrible — so I’ll do about the same. I’d rather put a little too much fertilizer than too little. Losing a crop hurts a lot more than wasting a few yuan on extra urea.
